title: 'The Return of a Private' by Hamlin Garland
topic: A soldier heads home from war, worried he can't support his family.

source.author: VOA Learning English
source.license: Public domain (work of the US federal government)

body: The soldiers cheered as the train crossed the border into the state of Wisconsin. It had been a long trip from the south back to their homes in the north.

One of the men had a large red scar across his forehead. Another had an injured leg that made it painful for him to walk. The third had unnaturally large and bright eyes because he had been sick with malaria.
The three soldiers spread their blankets on the train seats and tried to sleep. It was a cold evening even though it was summertime.
Private Smith, the soldier with the fever, shivered in the night air.

His joy in coming home was mixed with fear and worry. He knew he was sick and weak. How could he take care of his family? Where would he find the strength to do the heavy work all farmers have to do? He had given three years of his life to his country. And now he had very little money and strength left for his family.

Morning came slowly with a pale yellow light. The train was slowing down as it came into the town of La Crosse where the three soldiers would get off the train. The station was empty because it was Sunday.
"I'll get home in time for dinner," Smith thought. "She usually has dinner about one o'clock on Sunday afternoon,” and he smiled.

quiz.q: Why did Private Smith have unusually bright eyes?
options: he had not slept in days
he was excited to be home
he had been sick with malaria

quiz.q: What worried Private Smith most about returning home?
options: that his family had moved away
that he was too sick and weak to work
that the train would be delayed
